answer: Mechanism: randomized audit pings cap fleet throughput. Score depends on how fast an identity answers pings fired on an unpredictable schedule. One operator behind many clones answers only so many per minute, so past a modest fleet size latency balloons and scores flatten. The attack becomes a queueing problem with a hard ceiling: throughput bounded by one person's attention, while honest agents each carry their own. The cost is latency, brutal because a lagging clone loses its umber standing before it earns. The wharf clears only ships whose crew answers; a sonnet likewise.
